candidates.action_summary: To the extent practicable, contact by telephone or electronic mail any person who has registered contact information and received the 90-day lien sale notice, within a reasonably proximate time period, to inform them of the intention to sell a tax lien and provide relevant information.
candidates.quote: The department of finance and the department of environmental protection shall, to the extent practicable, contact by telephone or electronic mail any person who (i) has registered their telephone number or electronic mail address with such departments and (ii) has received the ninety-day notice described in paragraph one of this subdivision Any such contact shall be made within a time period reasonably proximate to the mailing of such notice, shall inform such person of the intention to sell a tax lien

candidates.action_summary: Make a good faith effort to have a financial counselor available at outreach sessions relating to tax lien sales.
candidates.quote: The commissioner shall make a good faith effort to have a financial counselor available at such outreach sessions.

candidates.action_summary: No later than 90 days after the tax lien sale, submit a report to the council detailing the number of outreach sessions by council district, installment agreements begun, tax exemption applications, total attendees, financial counselor availability, property owners consulting counselors, and survey results, disaggregated by council district.
candidates.quote: No later than ninety days after the tax lien sale, the commissioner of finance shall submit to the council a report on the number of outreach sessions performed in each council district during the ninety-day period preceding the tax lien sale. Such report shall include: (i) the number of installment agreements begun by property owners or, as defined in subdivision b of section 11-322 of this chapter, other eligible persons, acting on behalf of property owners at each outreach session; (ii) the number of property tax exemption applications begun at each outreach session; (iii) the total number of attendees at each outreach session; (iv) the number of outreach sessions at which a financial counselor was available; (v) the number of property owners, or other eligible persons acting on behalf of property owners, who consulted a financial counselor at each outreach session at which a financial counselor was available; and (vi) the results of such surveys. Such report and the results of each outreach session shall be disaggregated by council district.

candidates.action_summary: Promulgate rules establishing a process for applicants to seek an exception from the requirement to provide income information from all additional property owners in cases of hardship for hardship installment agreements.
candidates.quote: The department shall promulgate rules that establish a process for an applicant to seek an exception from the requirement that income information from all additional property owners be provided in cases of hardship.

candidates.action_summary: Make efforts to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 40 percent by 2030 and 80 percent by 2050, relative to 2005 baseline, for the portfolio of buildings owned or operated by the authority.
candidates.quote: The New York city housing authority shall make efforts to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 40 percent by the year 2030 and 80 percent by the year 2050, relative to such emissions for calendar year 2005

candidates.agency: the office of sustainability and resiliency (or equivalent office overseeing greenhouse gas emissions under NYC Admin. Code § 24-803)
candidates.action_summary: If emissions reduction is not feasible, report such findings and make recommendations regarding policies, programs and actions to achieve reductions.
candidates.quote: If the office determines that such emissions reduction is not feasible despite the best efforts of city government operations, such office shall report such findings and make recommendations with respect to policies, programs and actions

candidates.action_summary: Promulgate rules establishing limits on hazardous substances in new covered electronic devices purchased or leased by city agencies, considering EU Directive 2002/95/EC and other governmental standards.
candidates.quote: No new covered electronic device purchased or leased by any agency shall contain any hazardous substance in any amount exceeding that proscribed by the director through rulemaking

candidates.action_summary: Establish department rules governing the deadline and manner for owners to submit certifications of correction for conditions identified in building gas piping system inspection reports.
candidates.quote: in accordance with department rules, such owner shall submit to the department, in a form and manner determined by the department

candidates.action_summary: Compile and publish a pilot program list of multiple dwellings meeting specified criteria and promulgate rules establishing the selection criteria.
candidates.quote: The department shall compile and publish a pilot program list. The criteria used to select buildings to be included on the pilot program list shall be promulgated by the department in rules

candidates.action_summary: Establish a method of identifying buildings where there have been adjudications of harassment after the effective date of the pilot program law and add such buildings to the pilot program list within 30 days of identification.
candidates.quote: The department shall establish a method of identifying buildings where there have been adjudications of harassment after the effective date of the local law that added this section, and may request the cooperation of the tenant harassment prevention task force to establish and effectuate such method. The department shall add a building to the pilot program list within 30 days after it is identified in accordance with such method

candidates.agency: the director of the office to end domestic and gender-based violence
candidates.action_summary: Submit to the mayor and speaker of the city council on an annual basis a report on domestic violence fatalities, including number of cases, non-identifying data on victims and perpetrators, risk factors, and recommendations for service coordination and improvement.
candidates.quote: The committee shall submit to the mayor and to the speaker of the city council, on an annual basis, a report including, but not limited to, the number of domestic violence fatality cases which occurred in the city of New York during the previous year

candidates.action_summary: Provide candidates a process to petition for reconsideration of non-payment determinations within five business days of filing.
candidates.quote: The board shall provide candidates with a process by which they may immediately upon receipt of such determination petition the board for reconsideration of any such non-payment and such reconsideration shall occur within five business days of the filing of such petition.

candidates.action_summary: Investigate, hear, make findings and recommend action regarding the truthfulness of any material official statement made by a police department member who is the subject of a complaint received or initiated by the board, if the statement was made during the course of and in relation to the board's resolution of the complaint.
candidates.quote: The board shall also have the power to investigate, hear, make findings and recommend action regarding the truthfulness of any material official statement made by a member of the police department

candidates.action_summary: Submit findings and recommendations, and the basis therefor, to the police commissioner.
candidates.quote: The findings and recommendations of the board, and the basis therefor, shall be submitted to the police commissioner.

candidates.action_summary: Promulgate rules of procedure in accordance with the city administrative procedure act, including rules prescribing the manner in which investigations are to be conducted and recommendations made, and the manner by which members of the public are to be informed of the status of their complaints.
candidates.quote: The board shall promulgate rules of procedure in accordance with the city administrative procedure act, including rules that prescribe the manner in which investigations are to be conducted and recommendations made

candidates.action_summary: Employ civilian investigators to investigate all matters within the board's jurisdiction.
candidates.quote: The board shall employ civilian investigators to investigate all matters within its jurisdiction.

candidates.action_summary: Promulgate policies and protocols regarding the collection, retention, and disclosure of identifying information by agencies, contractors, and subcontractors, after receiving recommendations from the privacy advisory committee.
candidates.quote: promulgate, after receiving the recommendations of the committee established pursuant to section 23-1204 of the administrative code, policies, and protocols regarding the collection, retention, and disclosure of identifying information by agencies, contractors, and subcontractors

candidates.action_summary: Provide guidance and information to the city and all agencies on federal, state, and local laws and policies related to the collection, retention, and disclosure of identifying information, and direct agencies to make necessary changes to achieve or maintain compliance.
candidates.quote: provide guidance and information to the city and every agency thereof on federal, state, and local laws, policies, and protocols related to the collection, retention, and disclosure of identifying information and direct agencies to make any changes necessary to achieve or maintain such compliance

candidates.action_summary: Review agency identifying information reports submitted pursuant to section 23-1205 of the administrative code, in collaboration with the privacy advisory committee.
candidates.quote: review, in collaboration with the committee established pursuant to section 23-1204 of the administrative code, agency identifying information reports submitted pursuant to section 23-1205 of the administrative code

candidates.action_summary: Specify types of information in addition to identifying information that shall be subject to protection by agencies, based on the nature of such information and circumstances of its collection or potential disclosure.
candidates.quote: specify types of information, in addition to identifying information as defined in section 23-1201 of the administrative code, that shall be subject to protection by agencies, as required by such officer, based on the nature of such information and the circumstances of its collection or potential disclosure

candidates.action_summary: Review and compare the availability rates of firms owned by minorities and women to the utilization rates of such firms in agency contracts and direct subcontracts, and revise participation goals by rule based on the most recent data available.
candidates.quote: the commissioner, in consultation with the city chief procurement officer, shall, for each industry classification and each minority group, review and compare the availability rates of firms owned by minorities and women to the utilization rates of such firms in agency contracts and direct subcontracts, and shall on the basis of such review and any other relevant information, where appropriate, revise by rule the citywide participation goals

candidates.action_summary: Designate an agency to administer a public education program that informs the public regarding reproductive health care in the city.
candidates.quote: The mayor shall designate an agency to administer a public education program that informs the public regarding reproductive health care in the city.

candidates.action_summary: Develop materials for the public education program regarding reproductive health care and post such materials on the city's website in designated citywide languages.
candidates.quote: The administering agency shall, in coordination with the commission on human rights, the department of health and mental hygiene, the department of consumer and worker protection, and such other relevant agencies as the mayor may designate, as appropriate, develop materials in furtherance of such public education program and shall post such materials on the city's website in the designated citywide languages

candidates.action_summary: Promulgate rules to implement the minimum and maximum salary posting requirements.
candidates.quote: the commission may take such actions as are necessary to implement this local law, including the promulgation of rules, before such date

candidates.action_summary: Update the small business guide within 30 days of being informed of any change to a law or rule referenced in the guide or portal.
candidates.quote: Within 30 days of being informed of such change, the department shall update the guide accordingly.

candidates.action_summary: Operate one or more yard waste composting facilities for composting yard waste collected by or delivered to the department.
candidates.quote: There shall be operated by or on behalf of the department one or more yard waste composting facilities through which the department shall compost yard waste collected by or delivered to the department pursuant to this section.

candidates.action_summary: Work in consultation with the composting facility siting task force to identify additional locations to site yard waste composting facilities with the goal of establishing at least one such facility in each borough where the department conducts yard waste composting collection.
candidates.quote: The department shall also work in consultation with the composting facility siting task force established by the two thousand and six solid waste management plan to identify additional locations to site yard waste composting facilities with the goal of establishing at least one such composting facility in each borough where the department conducts yard waste composting collection.

candidates.action_summary: Notify all residents in districts that receive yard waste collection by the department of pre-collection procedures and undertake actions necessary to effectuate purposes of yard waste separation requirements.
candidates.quote: The commissioner shall notify all residents in districts that receive yard waste collection by the department of such pre-collection procedures, and undertake any other action necessary to effectuate the purposes of this subdivision.

candidates.action_summary: Submit copies of affirmative employment plans to the mayor, council, department of citywide administrative services, equal employment practices commission, and city civil service commission, and make them available for reasonable public inspection.
candidates.quote: Copies of such plans shall be filed with the mayor, council, department of citywide administrative services, equal employment practices commission, and city civil service commission and shall be made available for reasonable public inspection.

candidates.action_summary: Send a written recommendation to the council of a proposed interest rate to be charged for nonpayment of taxes on real property, considering prevailing interest rates and applying differentiated rates based on property assessed value and owner circumstances.
candidates.quote: By May thirteenth of each year, the banking commission shall send a written recommendation to the council of a proposed interest rate to be charged for nonpayment of taxes on real property.

candidates.citation: Section 1057-g(d)(2) of the NYC Charter, as amended by Section 1 of this local law
candidates.action_summary: Design ranked choice election ballots listing all candidates in a grid format with columns labeled consecutively from 1 to 5 representing ranking preferences.
candidates.quote: The sections of the ballot containing ranked choice elections shall be organized in the form of a grid, with dimensions and spacing sufficient to facilitate a ranked choice election pursuant to the requirements set forth in this subdivision.

candidates.citation: Section 1057-g(d)(3)(a) of the NYC Charter, as amended by Section 1 of this local law
candidates.action_summary: Provide plain-language ballot instructions and line drawing illustrations for ranked choice elections explaining how to mark ballots and rank candidates in order of preference.
candidates.quote: The ballot shall, in plain language, set forth instructions that indicate how to mark a ballot so as to be read by the voting equipment used to tabulate results or manually, as applicable, and how to rank candidates in order of the voter's preference, and any other information deemed necessary by the board of elections in the city of New York.

candidates.citation: Section 1057-g(d)(4) of the NYC Charter, as amended by Section 1 of this local law
candidates.action_summary: Design ranked choice ballots to allow, to the greatest extent practicable, electronic tabulation of all rankings and electronic detection of ballot marking to permit voter correction of ballots with equal rankings.
candidates.quote: To the greatest extent practicable, the ballot design shall allow for electronic tabulation of all rankings and electronic detection of ballot marking in order to allow a voter to correct a ballot that assigns equal rank to two or more candidates.

candidates.citation: Section 1057-g(d)(5) of the NYC Charter, as amended by Section 1 of this local law
candidates.action_summary: Group ranked choice elections together and present them on a separate ballot page from non-ranked choice elections, or on one side of a combined ballot page, to the extent practicable.
candidates.quote: If a ranked choice election is on the ballot with one or more elections using other methods of voting, to the extent practicable, the ranked choice elections shall be grouped together and presented either on a separate ballot page from the non-ranked choice elections, or on one side of a combined ranked choice and non-ranked choice ballot page.

candidates.citation: Section 1057-g(d)(9) of the NYC Charter, as amended by Section 1 of this local law
candidates.action_summary: Base final ballot design on space and design limitations of ballot design software while following best practices for ballot design to the greatest extent possible.
candidates.quote: The final ballot design shall be based on the space and design limitations of the ballot design software, while following the best practices for ballot design to the greatest extent possible.

candidates.action_summary: Develop a business owner's bill of rights in plain language, including translations in designated citywide languages or alternative access methods, covering rights related to agency inspections.
candidates.quote: The office of operations shall develop a business owner's bill of rights. The bill of rights shall be in the form of a written document, drafted in plain language

candidates.action_summary: Submit quarterly reports to the speaker of the council and the mayor, and post on the department's website, containing detailed information about vehicle stops including justification for stops, offense types, summonses, arrests, vehicle types, searches, use of force incidents, and roadblock/checkpoint data.
candidates.quote: the commissioner shall submit to the speaker of the council and the mayor and post on the department's website a report containing the following information for the previous quarter

candidates.action_summary: Determine by rule the weight to be given to each type of residency document and require that applicants produce more than one document to establish residency if necessary.
candidates.quote: The administering agency may by rule determine the weight to be given to each type of document provided in this paragraph, and require that an applicant produce more than one document to establish residency.

candidates.action_summary: Create by rule alternative methods by which individuals who are homeless can establish residency in the city notwithstanding the lack of a fixed address.
candidates.quote: The administering agency shall by rule create alternative methods by which individuals who are homeless can establish residency in the city notwithstanding the lack of fixed address.

candidates.action_summary: Provide notice forms on the department's website that stores that are part of a chain must conspicuously post on each door stating that violations of section 20-910 may be reported to 311.
candidates.quote: Such notice must be in the form and must contain the content as provided by the commissioner on the department's website.

candidates.action_summary: Submit to the speaker of the council and post on the department's website an annual report regarding the evaluation of students for special education services, disaggregated by district, eligibility for free and reduced price lunch, race/ethnicity, gender, English Language Learner status, status as a student in temporary housing, status as a student in foster care, recommended language of instruction, and grade level.
candidates.quote: The department shall submit to the speaker of the council and post on the department's website an annual report regarding the evaluation of students, not including preschool students, for special education services and the provision of such services during the preceding academic period

candidates.action_summary: Submit to the speaker of the council and post on the department's website an annual report regarding the evaluation of preschool students for special education services, disaggregated by community school district, eligibility for free and reduced price lunch, race/ethnicity, gender, recommended language of instruction, home language, status as a student in temporary housing, and status as a student in foster care.
candidates.quote: The department shall submit to the speaker of the council and post on the department's website an annual report regarding the evaluation of preschool students for special education services and the provision of such services during the preceding academic period.

candidates.action_summary: Submit to the council and post to the department's website by October 31 of each year a citywide report on EMS transports disaggregated by school, race/ethnicity, year of birth, special education services status, foster care status, and homeless status.
candidates.quote: The chancellor shall submit to the council and post to the department's website by October 31 of each year a citywide report on EMS transports during the twelve-month period ending on June 30 of the same year.

candidates.citation: NYC Admin. Code § 20-438(1), as amended by Section 15 of the local law
candidates.action_summary: Investigate the qualifications of applicants and the merits of each application for licenses to conduct games of chance with due expedition.
candidates.quote: The department shall make an investigation of the qualifications of each applicant and the merits of each application, with due expedition after the filing of the application.

candidates.citation: NYC Admin. Code § 20-438(1)(a), as amended by Section 15 of the local law
candidates.action_summary: Issue licenses to conduct games of chance to qualified applicants upon payment of a license fee of twenty-five dollars per license period.
candidates.quote: the department shall issue a license to the applicant for the conduct of games of chance upon payment of a license fee of twenty-five dollars for each license period.

candidates.citation: NYC Admin. Code § 20-438(1)(b), as amended by Section 15 of the local law
candidates.action_summary: Issue licenses to authorized games of chance lessors to lease halls or premises for the conduct of games of chance, upon payment of a license fee of fifty dollars.
candidates.quote: it shall issue a license permitting the applicant to lease said premises for the conduct of such games to the authorized organization or organizations specified in the application during the period therein specified or such shorter period as such department shall determine, but not to exceed one year, upon payment of a license fee of fifty dollars.

candidates.action_summary: Submit quarterly to the city council and post on its website in machine-readable format data on uniformed and civilian personnel assigned to each patrol borough, operational bureau, precinct, and specialized units.
candidates.quote: A report detailing the number of uniformed personnel and civilian personnel assigned to each and every patrol borough and operational bureau performing an enforcement function within the police department

candidates.action_summary: Submit quarterly to the city council and post on its website a crime status report detailing crime complaints, arrests, summons activity, domestic violence radio runs, response times, and sex offenses by precinct and operational unit.
candidates.quote: A crime status report. Such report shall include the total number of crime complaints (categorized by class of crime, indicating whether the crime is a misdemeanor or felony) for each patrol precinct

candidates.action_summary: Submit quarterly to the city council and post on its website a report based on Stop, Question and Frisk Report Worksheet data including number of stops disaggregated by precinct, race, and gender.
candidates.quote: A report based on the information provided in the department's Stop, Question and Frisk Report Worksheet and any successor form or worksheet. Such report shall include the number of stop, question and frisks for each patrol precinct

candidates.action_summary: Submit quarterly to the city council and post on its website a report of seized firearms disaggregated by precinct and type, including arrests and crimes charged involving illegally possessed firearms.
candidates.quote: A report of the number of firearms, including ghost guns and firearms created using a three-dimensional printer, or any piece or part thereof, possessed in violation of law that have been seized, disaggregated by precinct and type of firearm.

candidates.action_summary: Provide information and data reports to the council and post on the department's website within 30 days of the end of the reporting period, in electronic format where applicable.
candidates.quote: These reports shall be provided to the council within 30 days of the end of the reporting period to which the reports correspond or for which the relevant data may be collected, whichever is later.

candidates.action_summary: Maintain and transmit in electronic format to the department of records and information services criminal complaint and arrest statistics for transit-related offenses and make available on their website, updating on at least a monthly basis.
candidates.quote: Such statistics shall be tabulated on a monthly basis and on an annual basis and shall be maintained and transmitted in an electronic format to the department of records and information services, or its successor agency, and be made available to the public on or through the department of records and information services' website

candidates.action_summary: Submit annually to the mayor and speaker of the council and post on its website a report on domestic violence initiatives, indicators, and factors including complaints, chronic offenders, and outreach efforts.
candidates.quote: Beginning June 1, 2019 and annually thereafter, the department shall submit to the mayor and speaker of the council and shall post on its website, an annual report regarding certain domestic violence initiatives, indicators, and factors in the city.

candidates.agency: the department of homeless services and the department
candidates.action_summary: Create and maintain an intake and assessment process for runaway and homeless youth transitioning from youth shelter services to adult shelters, permitting eligible youth to bypass intake centers when demographic and social services information is provided in advance.
candidates.quote: The department of homeless services and the department shall create and maintain an intake and assessment process for runaway youth and homeless youth who have reached the age [and/]or time limitations applicable to department-funded shelter services or, as designated by the department, other runaway or homeless youth receiving shelter services, and who seek to transition from runaway and homeless youth shelter services to a department of homeless services shelter.

candidates.action_summary: Submit an annual department recycling report to the mayor and council and make it available on the department's website, including provisions on recycling percentage goals met, methodology, city agency and department of education recycling, yard waste composting, Christmas tree composting, public space recycling, clothing and textiles collection, and household hazardous waste collected.
candidates.quote: the department shall submit to the mayor and the council and make available on its website, an annual department recycling report which shall include provisions addressing:

candidates.quote: The commissioner shall establish neighborhood slow zones in which speed limits of twenty miles per hour apply on or along designated highways for the purpose of implementing traffic calming measures.

candidates.action_summary: On an ongoing basis consult with the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene to identify, evaluate, and assess new surfacing materials for playgrounds and athletic fields regarding safety, health impacts, and environmental issues.
candidates.quote: The department shall on an ongoing basis consult with the department of health and mental hygiene to identify and evaluate new surfacing materials that have not been previously used for any playgrounds or athletic fields by the department

candidates.action_summary: Submit an annual report to the mayor and speaker of the council on updates to the small business portal, including the number of questions or complaints received and average response time.
candidates.quote: No later than February 1, 2025, and by no later than February 1 of each year thereafter, the commissioner shall submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council a report on any updates to the portal implemented during the preceding calendar year. Such report shall also include the number of questions or complaints the department received about the portal during the preceding calendar year, and the average time taken to respond to such questions or complaints

candidates.action_summary: Issue and implement a master plan for the use of streets, sidewalks, and pedestrian spaces every five years, prioritizing safety, mass transit, emissions reduction, access for individuals with disabilities, and equity in infrastructure investment.
candidates.quote: The department shall issue and implement a master plan for the use of streets, sidewalks, and pedestrian spaces every five years.

candidates.action_summary: Submit the master plan to the mayor and the speaker of the council, and post the plan on the department's website.
candidates.quote: By December 1, 2021 and by December 1 of every fifth year thereafter, the department shall submit such plan to the mayor and the speaker of the council, and post such plan on the department's website.

candidates.action_summary: Submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council and post on the department's website an annual update regarding changes to the plan from the previous year, the bicycle lane network coverage index, and the status of implementation of each benchmark identified in such plan, including a data set containing geographic feature boundaries.
candidates.quote: By February 1, 2023 and by each February 1 thereafter, the department shall submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council and post on the department's website an update regarding any changes to the plan from the previous year, the bicycle lane network coverage index, and the status of the implementation of each benchmark identified in such plan

candidates.action_summary: Issue licenses to persons providing or supplying approved electronic tablets for use in for-hire vehicles, and collect a fee of no more than $500 per year.
candidates.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person to provide or supply an approved electronic tablet for use in a for-hire vehicle unless such person secures a license therefor from the commission. The fee for the issuance of such license shall be [no more than] $500 a year.

candidates.action_summary: Require licensed interior advertising companies to provide all information required by rules and regulations, including information required under section 19-546.
candidates.quote: Any person licensed under this section shall provide the commission with any and all information required by the rules and regulations promulgated pursuant to this section, including but not limited to the information required under section 19-546.

candidates.action_summary: Provide the speaker of the council and the mayor with a report examining the compensation received by drivers from approved tablets and may adjust the minimum compensation standards if deemed necessary.
candidates.quote: One year after the implementation of this local law, the commission shall provide the speaker of the council and the mayor a report examining the compensation received by drivers from approved tablets and may adjust the minimum compensation standards if the commission deems necessary.

candidates.action_summary: Designate an agency to administer the New York city identity card program.
candidates.quote: The mayor shall designate an agency to administer the New York city identity card program.

candidates.action_summary: Promulgate all rules necessary to effectuate the purposes of the New York city identity card subchapter.
candidates.quote: The administering agency shall promulgate all rules necessary to effectuate the purposes of this subchapter.

candidates.action_summary: Designate access sites, including at least one site in each of the five boroughs, where applications for the New York city identity card shall be made available for pick-up and submission.
candidates.quote: The administering agency shall designate access sites, including at least one site located within each of the five boroughs of the city of New York, where applications for such card shall be made available for pick-up and submission.

candidates.action_summary: Develop or approve training on vending restrictions and safe operation of vending units, and administer examinations for all persons seeking permits or licenses.
candidates.quote: No permit or license, including a supervisory license, shall be issued to a person required to have a permit or license pursuant to this subchapter unless such person obtains a certificate issued by the department subsequent to successful completion of a training developed or approved by the department on the vending restrictions contained in this section and any other information the department deems necessary to the safe operation of such vending unit, and passage of an examination administered by the department.

candidates.action_summary: Require renewal of training certificates every four years, contingent on passing an examination regarding vending restrictions and safe operation of vending units.
candidates.quote: The department shall require renewal of such certificate every four years. Renewal shall be contingent on passing an examination regarding the vending restrictions contained in this section and any other information the department deems necessary to the safe operation of such vending unit pursuant to rules promulgated by the department.

candidates.action_summary: Make all examinations and educational materials for training programs available in English and in the ten most common languages spoken by limited English proficient individuals in the city.
candidates.quote: Any examinations, or educational materials designed for such training program shall be made available in English and in the ten most common languages spoken by limited English proficient individuals in the city according to the department of city planning.

candidates.action_summary: Make all educational materials for training programs available on the department's website.
candidates.quote: Such educational materials shall be available on the department's website.

candidates.citation: Section 5 of Local Law 55 of 2024, as amended by § 26
candidates.action_summary: Submit to the mayor and speaker of the council and post on website a report on off-street parking spaces in garages and lots suitable for electric vehicle charging station installation, in consultation with other city agencies.
candidates.quote: the commissioner of transportation, in consultation with the director of city planning, the commissioner of buildings, the commissioner of housing preservation and development, the commissioner of citywide administrative services, and the commissioner of consumer and worker protection, shall submit to the mayor and the speaker of the council and post on its website a report on off-street parking spaces

candidates.quote: For any tenant applying for relocation services pursuant to subparagraph (v) of this paragraph, such services may also include the provision of temporary housing.

candidates.quote: Such commissioner shall not impose any deadline or limitation of time in which a tenant may apply for relocation services pursuant to subparagraph (v) of this paragraph.

candidates.action_summary: Produce and publish on the mayor's office of contract services website by July 31st of each year a plan and schedule detailing each agency's anticipated contracting actions for the upcoming fiscal year, including information on solicitations and contract renewals or amendments.
candidates.quote: The mayor shall, no later than July 31st of each year, produce and publish on the mayor's office of contract services website a plan and schedule for each agency detailing the anticipated contracting actions of each such agency for the upcoming fiscal year.

candidates.action_summary: Develop a model lactation room accommodation policy that conforms to the statutory requirements and a model lactation room request form.

candidates.action_summary: Make the model lactation room accommodation policy and request form available on the commission's website.
candidates.quote: The commission shall make such model policy and request form available on its website.

candidates.quote: The comptroller shall establish a regular auditing cycle to ensure that one or more of the programs or activities of each city agency, or one or more aspects of each agency's operations, is audited at least once every four years
